newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up in active trade.

text.p: Despite several bouts of profit-taking, especially in the afternoon, Thai stocks ended up slightly in active trade as locals and mutual funds snapped up cheap blue-chip stocks, brokers said.

"Market sentiment today remained bearish as there was no positive news to stimulate investment at all. The buying was purely for speculative reasons after the market fell sharply on Friday," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance.
The composite SET index, which fell to a new eight-year low on Friday, finished up 3.84 points to 534.46 on 9.8 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index rose 0.39 point to 38.15. Decliners led gainers 159 to 124 while 89 issues remained unchanged.

Monday's buying focused mainly on banking, communication and finance counters. The banking sector topped the active list, rising 2.62 percent, followed by the communication sector advancing 1.42 percent and the finance counter surging 0.30 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, gaining four baht to 146. BEC World advanced four to 220 and Shinawatra Computer lost 10 to 104.
